scope: Specific museum objects, translated passages, scholarly analyses, institutional descriptions and empirical studies are distinguished. No fresh manuscript collation, complete reading of abstract-only books, genetic proof of cultural descent or population survey is claimed.

sources.title: British Museum, Papyrus of Ani, EA10470,3
sources.locator: Judgment vignette, frame 3
sources.scope: The heart, Ma'at, scales, Anubis and divine record are described by the collection. This is a particular funerary witness, not every Egyptian person's creed.

sources.title: British Museum, Greenfield Papyrus, EA10554,80
sources.locator: Spell 125 and judgment vignette; approximately 950-930 BCE
sources.scope: The described vignette includes Ma'at, judgment, Ammit and a lake of fire. Its combination cautions against reducing all Egyptian punishment accounts to one formula.

sources.title: UCL Petrie Museum, Pyramid Text
sources.kind: Institutional artifact description with translated meaning
sources.locator: Pepy I pyramid inscription, Sixth Dynasty
sources.scope: The museum identifies formulae assisting royal ascent to heaven and continued sustenance. The royal setting is preserved rather than projected onto all Egyptians.

sources.title: UCL Digital Egypt, Pyramid Texts
sources.locator: Unas and later reuse
sources.scope: The page distinguishes earliest monumental attestations from subsequent reuse on other objects. The modern corpus name is not one author's title.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Book of the Dead of Imhotep
sources.locator: Early Ptolemaic, approximately 332-200 BCE
sources.scope: A specific priestly manuscript demonstrates continued Egyptian funerary textual production in the Ptolemaic era; this does not establish every proposed Hermetic borrowing.

sources.title: Jasnow and Zauzich, The Ancient Egyptian Book of Thoth, Johns Hopkins description
sources.kind: Institutional description of a critical edition
sources.locator: 2005 edition; Demotic witnesses and House of Life
sources.scope: Description of dispersed manuscripts, master-disciple dialogue and scribal knowledge was consulted. The complete edition was not read; the suggested Hermetic relationship remains the editors' research comparison.

sources.title: Jasnow and Zauzich, The Ancient Egyptian Book of Thoth II
sources.kind: Institutional description of a critical-edition supplement
sources.locator: 2021 supplement; 89 additional fragments
sources.scope: The description establishes added witnesses and revised reconstruction, not a full independent reading of those fragments in this project.

sources.title: Richard Jasnow, The Book of Thoth (2017)
sources.locator: Religion Compass, DOI 10.1111/rec3.12236
sources.scope: Abstract-level evidence for priestly learning, House of Life and ritual context. No claim of access to the whole article is made.

sources.title: Plato, Phaedrus, Benjamin Jowett translation
sources.locator: Theuth and Thamus, 274c-275b; dialectical collection and division, 265d-266b
sources.scope: Explicit Egyptian literary framing is distinct from evidence that Plato personally received these doctrines at a temple. The interlocutors' treatment of storytelling remains part of the passage.

sources.title: Plato, Timaeus, Benjamin Jowett translation
sources.locator: Solon and Sais, 21e-25d; goodness of the maker, 29e-30a
sources.scope: The dialogue supplies its own literary appeal to Egyptian antiquity and a good cosmological maker. It does not supply an independently verified history of Atlantis or a doctrine that all matter is evil.

sources.title: Plato, Republic X, Benjamin Jowett translation
sources.locator: Myth of Er, 614b-621d
sources.scope: Judgment, posthumous recompense, choice and return are compared. No Egyptian source is named as the origin of this particular story within the consulted passage.

sources.title: Strabo on Egyptian priests and Plato, translated extract introduced by Philip Harland
sources.kind: Primary historical testimony in a scholar's translation
sources.locator: Geography 17.1.29, indexed passage
sources.scope: The indexed extract reports places associated with Plato and Eudoxus and attributes the duration of study to earlier writers. Direct full-page access failed. It is later testimony, not Strabo's eyewitness observation of Plato.

sources.title: J. Paul Getty Museum, Golden Tickets to the Underworld
sources.locator: Gold tablet 75.AM.19, approximately 350-300 BCE
sources.scope: Instruction, identity, memory and a special posthumous destination are attested in a particular Greek ritual witness. Orphic is not used as proof of one uniform ancient denomination.

sources.title: Brian P. Copenhaver, Hermetica, Introduction
sources.locator: Greek-Egyptian religious and cultural setting
sources.scope: Available summary, not a fresh full reading of the translated collection. The philosophical Hermetica must not all be assigned to the founding of Alexandria.

sources.title: Plotinus, Enneads V, MacKenna and Page translation
sources.scope: One, Intellect, Soul, procession and the discussion of Egyptian representations provide different comparisons. Overflow is not treated as measured light becoming denser matter.

sources.title: Plotinus, Enneads II, MacKenna and Page translation
sources.locator: II.9, conventionally Against the Gnostics
sources.scope: The defense of the cosmos and criticism of rivals prevents treating every creator-critical text as an adoption of Plotinus's own doctrine.

sources.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Plotinus
sources.locator: Biography and metaphysics
sources.scope: The third-century CE setting and philosophical distinction among hypostases are used; this is not empirical physics or a historical account of every later school.

sources.title: Peter Adamson, The Theology of Aristotle, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.locator: Arabic Plotinus, al-Kindi circle and later reception
sources.scope: The identified paraphrase of Enneads IV-VI and its transformations supply a concrete transmission example. The route does not imply every Muslim mystic read the same book.

sources.title: Institute of Ismaili Studies, Universal Intellect glossary
sources.locator: Universal Intellect and Universal Soul in an Ismaili account
sources.scope: A specified cosmological formulation, not a universal survey of present Nizari belief.

sources.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite
sources.locator: Late antique Christian appropriation of Neoplatonism
sources.scope: A concrete Christian case of hierarchy and return; apostolic authorship is distinguished from the later authorial setting.

sources.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Suhrawardi
sources.locator: Illuminationism, hierarchy of lights and methods of knowledge
sources.scope: The school is a productive additional comparison, not proof of a single secret organization or an exclusively anti-rational method.

sources.title: Gerhard Bowering, Baqa wa fana, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.kind: Specialist study using named Sufi witnesses
sources.locator: Passing away, transformed attributes and subsistence
sources.scope: Different uses of self-effacement are retained. The term is not equated universally with the literal destruction of a person or the abolishing of ethical responsibility.

sources.title: Abdu'l-Baha, Some Answered Questions
sources.locator: Chapters 37-39, especially 37.5 and 38.5
sources.scope: The mirror analogy rejects divine incarnation into the mirror and describes human souls as originated yet enduring. This supports comparison of mediation while resisting an automatic imprisoned-fragment reading.

sources.title: Hiroshi Murakami, Cathar Philosophy and Creationism (2020)
sources.locator: Book of Two Principles and absolute dualism
sources.scope: An explicitly identified medieval text and a scholar's interpretation. The full Japanese article was not read, and neither every Cathar accusation nor a direct Bogomil genealogy is established.

sources.title: AMORC, History of the Rosicrucian Order
sources.locator: Early modern manifestos and claimed heritage
sources.scope: The historical reference to the manifestos and the order's own lineage claims are separate. A present claim of ancient continuity is not independent confirmation of that continuity.

sources.title: The Theosophical Society, Mission and Objects
sources.locator: Objects and freedom of thought
sources.scope: The society's public commitments are distinguished from compulsory assent to every doctrine associated with Blavatsky or later esoteric teachers.

sources.title: British Museum and Smarthistory, Lapis lazuli stamp seal
sources.locator: Eastern Iranian seal, approximately 2400-2000 BCE; material distribution
sources.scope: Trade and material circulation support opportunities for contact, not a demonstrated itinerary for a judgment myth. Provenance of individual lapis objects and the origins of Zoroastrianism are different questions.

sources.title: Asha, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.locator: Avestan asha and Indo-Iranian cognates
sources.scope: The linguistic relationship with Vedic rta is evidence distinct from a functional comparison with Ma'at. Cultural exchange does not require linguistic kinship, but analogy does not establish etymology.

sources.title: Ahmad Tafazzoli, Cinwad Puhl, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.kind: Specialist analysis of different textual strata
sources.locator: Gathic bridge references and later Middle Persian judgment accounts
sources.scope: The scales, tribunal and bridge motifs are not all projected without qualification onto one original moment or one author.

sources.title: Homer, Odyssey XI, Samuel Butler translation
sources.locator: Achilles and the punished figures in the same book
sources.scope: A shadowy general condition coexists with special punishments. One famous remark by Achilles does not represent every posthumous fate in Homer.

sources.title: Homer, Odyssey IV, Samuel Butler translation
sources.locator: Menelaus and Elysium
sources.scope: A privileged destination precedes Plato in the literary tradition; it is not automatically a universal ethical reward system.

sources.title: Oxford ETCSL, Gilgamesh, Enkidu and the nether world
sources.kind: Primary literary text in scholarly translation
sources.locator: Final questions about the dead and the living's care
sources.scope: Differences related to descendants, burial and offerings challenge the claim that a shadowy afterlife eliminates transgenerational concerns.

sources.title: Kokugakuin University, Encyclopedia of Shinto: View of the Other World
sources.locator: Different accounts of the world after death
sources.scope: Diversity and later interpretation are preserved; the entry is not a survey that every present Shinto practitioner believes one morally neutral underground fate.

sources.title: Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus
sources.locator: Death, sensation and prudent living
sources.scope: A clearer ancient comparison for death without experience than a populated realm of shades. It does not prove a direct line to a particular modern atheist.

sources.title: Daniel 12, World English Bible
sources.scope: Differentiated awakening and enduring outcomes are explicit. This passage alone does not establish the source of every motif or the composition date of all books mentioning Sheol.

sources.title: Zaval, Markowitz and Weber, How Will I Be Remembered? Conserving the Environment for the Sake of One's Legacy (2015)
sources.locator: Psychological Science; legacy motivation and environmental decisions
sources.scope: Reported association and experimental legacy intervention concern specified outcomes, not proof that moral afterlives caused modern environmentalism or that the effect is universal.

sources.title: Purzycki and colleagues, Moralistic gods, supernatural punishment and the expansion of human sociality (2016)
sources.locator: Eight communities, 591 participants and allocation games
sources.scope: Associations involving distant co-religionists are not equivalent to universal altruism, an environmental intervention or a complete historical causal genealogy.

sources.title: Humanists International, The Amsterdam Declaration (2022)
sources.locator: Human flourishing, other beings and future generations
sources.scope: A declared secular ethic demonstrates a non-afterlife route to future concern. It is not an empirical measure of every atheist's conduct or a denial of all religious influence.

sources.title: Integral Life, Pre/trans fallacy
sources.locator: Pre-rational and trans-rational as different categories
sources.scope: A modern interpretive vocabulary, not an independently validated periodization of Egypt, Greece or indigenous societies.
